title: Hang a hamster's water bottle on its wire cage with the spout through the bars
instruction: Hang the water bottle on the cage so the hamster can drink from the spout.
context: Hamsters, gerbils, guinea pigs and rabbits are commonly kept in wire cages with a hanging sipper bottle, which comes off for refilling every day or two. Put back wrong, the pet has no water: the sipper tube must reach in through the bars at a height it can drink from, and the hanger must sit on a cage wire. Real 8 oz bottle and steel hanger, common wire-top cage.
setup: World: x away from the robot, y to its left, z up; bench top z 0.7475 m. Cage (2.0 kg, free on the bench, not turned): a wire-top hamster cage 460 mm long, 290 mm deep, 271 mm tall. Its front wall faces the robot with its bar plane at x 0.420 m. Blue plastic base: 8 mm floor (the cage floor is 8 mm above the bench), walls up to a rim 69.35 mm above the bench. Zinc-plated steel wire 2.5 mm thick. Front wall: vertical bars with 12.0 mm clear between them (14.5 mm pitch, gaps centred at multiples of 14.5 mm from the wall's middle), from the rim to the top. Horizontal wires welded on the outside of the bars, centres 70.6 mm (just above the rim), 220.5 mm (the high wire) and 270.0 mm (the top frame) above the bench. A door opening from 40 to 120 mm left of the wall's middle and 95 to 250 mm up, framed by 8 mm wide flat steel strips standing 6 mm proud of the bars; the high wire stops at the door frame. Bottle: a Kaytee Clear 8 oz small-pet water bottle, filled: clear oval body 44 x 57 mm and 112 mm long, a 30 mm blue cap and an 8 mm stainless sipper tube 50 mm long with a ball tip; 0.39 kg with the water and the hanger. Hanger: black epoxy-coated 4 mm steel, a band round the body 30 mm above the cap and a rigid arm up to a hook (an 18 mm top bar and a 12 mm lip) that holds the bottle 35 degrees from vertical, spout toward the cage, when the hook sits on a horizontal wire. Drip stand (0.6 kg, white): a 100 x 110 x 8 mm base, two posts and a 70 x 84 x 6 mm plate 75 mm above the bench with a 34 x 36 mm hole. The bottle stands spout-down in it, the cap and tube through the hole, the body's 44 mm depth along x, the hanger's arm toward the cage. Lot A: cage middle at y -0.120 m; stand centre (0.240, -0.200) m. Lot B: cage middle at y -0.316 m (its door now where lot A's bottle hangs); stand centre (0.240, -0.330) m. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial, 1.0 when all of these hold together, with both hands more than 5 mm from the bottle and its hanger and the bottle and cage still within 1 mm for 1 s: the hanger's hook rests on top of the front wall's high horizontal wire (the wire lies under the hook's 18 mm top bar, at least 2 mm in from either end, with the bar's underside 1.0 mm below to 1.5 mm above the wire's top, away from the door); the sipper tube's tip is at least 8 mm inside the bar plane (and at least 10 mm in from the cage's sides and back) and 40 to 60 mm above the cage floor; the tube points down at least 20 degrees below level; and the body's lower edge on the cage side rests against the bars (within 6 mm of the bar plane). 0 otherwise, including a bottle still held, hung with the tube outside the bars, hung on another wire or the door frame, or not hung. Whole trial: if the cage is ever pushed more than 10 mm or tipped more than 3 degrees from where it started, or the hands, bottle or cage cannot be read at any step, the trial scores 0. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 800 control steps (40 seconds at 20 Hz) per trial; trials on lots A and B, averaged (--epochs 2).
reset_notes: 1. Lift the bottle so its hook clears the high wire, then draw it back along the tube until the tube is out of the bars. 2. Stand it spout-down in the drip stand, hanger arm toward the cage. 3. Set the cage and the stand on the lot's tape marks: lot A cage middle at y -0.120 m and stand at (0.240, -0.200) m; lot B cage middle at y -0.316 m and stand at (0.240, -0.330) m; the cage's front bar plane at x 0.420 m in both. Nothing is consumed; top up the water if any dripped.
fidelity: True-size bottle, hanger and cage wire, rigid bodies with real contact. Water is a fixed mass. The oval body is an octagonal prism, the ball tip a plain tube end, the hanger a rigid 4 mm rod (the real one is spring steel). Bottle size is the maker's listing; cap, tube and hanger shapes and the cage's wire heights and door are estimates to measure. The cage is one rigid 2 kg body. Lots stop a fixed replay, not memorising both layouts.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (lot A 1.0, lot B 1.0). Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lot A 0.0, lot B 0.0; step limit both). object_jitter=0, --epochs 2.
